    const l = grow(depth - 1);

    pool[2 * me] = l;
    pool[2 * me + 1] = r;
  } else {

 * binary-trees benchmark (TypeScript)
 *
 * Allocates and deallocates many perfect binary trees to exercise memory
 * management, then prints node-count checksums:
 *
 *   - one "stretch" tree of depth N+1 (built, checked, released),
 *   - for each even depth d = 4, 6, ..., N: 2^(N-d+4) short-lived trees of
 *     depth d (built, checked, released, checksums accumulated),
 *   - one long-lived tree of depth N (built up front, checked last).
 *
 * Memory strategy: all nodes live in one preallocated Int32Array arena.
 * A node i stores its child indices in pool[2i] / pool[2i+1] (-1 = leaf).
 * Allocation is bump-pointer; every tree occupies one contiguous block, so
 * releasing a tree is an O(1) reset of the bump pointer. This keeps the
 * workload allocation-heavy (every node of every tree is written and later
 * re-written by the next tree) while avoiding GC pauses.
 */

const parsed = parseInt(process.argv[2] || '', 10);
const N = parsed >= 0 ? parsed : 18;

// tree (2^(N+1)-1 nodes) plus the biggest short-lived tree (<= 2^(N+1)-1
// nodes) coexist and fit in the same capacity.
const capacity = Math.pow(2, N + 2) - 1;
const pool = new Int32Array(2 * capacity);

let top = 0; // arena bump pointer (index of next free node)

/** Bottom-up construction of a perfect tree of the given depth; returns root. */
function grow(depth: number): number {
  const me = top++;
  if (depth > 0) {
    const l = grow(depth - 1);
    const r = grow(depth - 1);
    pool[2 * me] = l;
    pool[2 * me + 1] = r;
  } else {
    pool[2 * me] = -1;
    pool[2 * me + 1] = -1;
  }
  return me;
}

function check(root: number): number {
  const l = pool[2 * root];
  if (l < 0) return 1;
  return 1 + check(l) + check(pool[2 * root + 1]);
}

const stretchRoot = grow(N + 1);

}

 * binary-trees — allocate, walk and deallocate many binary trees.
 *
 * Given N (first command-line argument):
 *   1. build a "stretch" tree of depth N+1, check it, release it;
 *   2. build a "long-lived" tree of depth N and keep it;
 *   3. for each even depth d = 4, 6, ..., N build 2^(N-d+4) short-lived
 *      trees of depth d, checking and releasing each one;
 *   4. check the long-lived tree last.
 *
 * The check of a tree is its node count, computed by a full traversal of
 * the child links (never from the depth alone).
 *
 * Memory strategy: a single preallocated Int32Array arena holds every node;
 * node i keeps its two child indices in pool[2i] and pool[2i+1] (-1 = leaf).
 * Each tree is placed in one contiguous block (preorder bump allocation)
 * and is deallocated by handing the block back for reuse, so the arena is
 * rewritten continuously — allocation-heavy, pause-free, cache-friendly.
 */

const parsed = parseInt(process.argv[2] || '', 10);
const N: number = parsed >= 0 ? parsed : 18;

// Arena capacity: the stretch tree (2^(N+2)-1 nodes) is the largest single
// allocation; later the long-lived tree (2^(N+1)-1) and the biggest
// short-lived tree (<= 2^(N+1)-1) coexist and also fit.
const pool = new Int32Array(2 * (Math.pow(2, N + 2) - 1));

/**
 * Allocate a perfect tree of the given depth into the arena block that
 * starts at `base` and return the index of its root. The block spans
 * 2^(depth+1)-1 nodes, linked bottom-up with explicit child indices.
 */
function grow(base: number, depth: number): number {
  if (depth > 0) {
    const rightBase = base + (1 << depth); // left subtree holds 2^depth-1 nodes
    const left = grow(base + 1, depth - 1);
    const right = grow(rightBase, depth - 1);
    pool[2 * base] = left;
    pool[2 * base + 1] = right;
  } else {
    pool[2 * base] = -1;
    pool[2 * base + 1] = -1;
  }
  return base;
}

/** Node-count checksum: full traversal via the stored child links. */
function check(root: number): number {
  const left = pool[2 * root];
  if (left < 0) return 1;
  return 1 + check(left) + check(pool[2 * root + 1]);
}

/**
 * binary-trees — allocate, walk, and deallocate many binary trees.
 *
 * Input:  N (non-negative integer) as the first command-line argument.
 *
 * Workload:
 *   1. build a "stretch" tree of depth N+1, check it, release it;
 *   2. build a "long-lived" tree of depth N and keep it alive;
 *   3. for each even depth d = 4, 6, ..., N, build 2^(N-d+4) short-lived
 *      trees of depth d, checking and releasing each one;
 *   4. check the long-lived tree last.
 *
 * The check of a tree is its node count, obtained by a full traversal of
 * the child links (never derived from the depth).
 *
 * Memory strategy: all nodes live in one preallocated Int32Array arena.
 * Node i stores its two child indices at pool[2i] and pool[2i+1]; -1 marks
 * a leaf. Every tree is placed in one contiguous block (preorder bump
 * placement) and is deallocated by returning the block for reuse, so the
 * arena is rewritten continuously: allocation-heavy, cache-friendly, and
 * free of GC pauses.
 */

const parsed = parseInt(process.argv[2] || '', 10);
const N: number = parsed >= 0 ? parsed : 18;

// Arena capacity: the stretch tree (2^(N+2)-1 nodes) is the largest single
// allocation. Later, the long-lived tree (2^(N+1)-1 nodes) and the biggest
// short-lived tree (at most 2^(N+1)-1 nodes) coexist and also fit.
const pool = new Int32Array(2 * (Math.pow(2, N + 2) - 1));

/**
 * Allocate a perfect tree of the given depth into the arena block starting
 * at `base` (the block spans 2^(depth+1)-1 nodes) and return the root index.
 * Children are linked explicitly, bottom-up.
 */
function grow(base: number, depth: number): number {
  if (depth > 0) {
    const rightBase = base + (1 << depth); // left subtree spans 2^depth-1 nodes
    const left = grow(base + 1, depth - 1);
    const right = grow(rightBase, depth - 1);
    pool[2 * base] = left;
    pool[2 * base + 1] = right;
  } else {
    pool[2 * base] = -1;
    pool[2 * base + 1] = -1;
  }
  return base;
}

/** Node-count checksum: full traversal via the stored child links. */
function check(root: number): number {
  const left = pool[2 * root];
  if (left < 0) return 1;
  return 1 + check(left) + check(pool[2 * root + 1]);
}

const out: string[] = [];

// 1. Stretch tree of depth N+1: build, check, release (its block is reused).
grow(0, N + 1);
out.push(`stretch tree of depth ${N + 1}\t check: ${check(0)}`);

// 2. Long-lived tree of depth N: occupies the low part of the arena and is
//    kept alive until the very end.
grow(0, N);
const shortBase = Math.pow(2, N + 1) - 1; // first node above the long-lived tree

//    reuses the same block above the long-lived tree (allocate -> check ->
//    release).

  for (let i = 0; i < iterations; i++) {
    grow(shortBase, d);

}
